Subject: Context-length discount mapping and token crediting — walkthrough

Emma — thanks for the call earlier. Per follow-up, I wanted to put pen to paper on how the 20% committed discount in the term sheet maps to token accounting when customers send long-context requests (single-call >16k tokens) and how rounding/minimums interact. Attaching a short example spreadsheet and a sample invoice for reference.

High-level summary up front:
- Commit discount (20%) applies to billable token units after rounding is applied per our metering quantum (256 tokens).
- Long single-call contexts are split at the metering layer into billable quanta; we do not charge an additional "long-context premium" — the cost is the same unit price, aggregated across the request.
- There is a monthly minimum (committed units) that BrightCart agreed to; any shortfall is billed at the discounted unit price and reconciled monthly.

Concrete examples are in the attached spreadsheet (sheet: 'examples'). I included three rows: short chat, long single-call with 48k tokens, and interleaved microbursts. The math shows our rounding (ceil to 256 tokens) and how the 20% off list rate is applied post-rounding.

Open items for your team to confirm:
1) Do you want the commit floor applied before or after prefix-based KV caching credits? (We typically apply commit floor to net billed units after credits.)
2) For invoice presentation: do you prefer a single line item for "compute tokens (post-discounts)" or granular lines per call type?

If that looks right I can draft language for the SOW and invoice examples later today.

— Markus

Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — spreadsheet helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our finance and engineering teams:  

- When you say "ceil to 256 tokens" — do you apply that per request chunk after you split for model sequence length limits, or per logical call? Example: if our app streams a 48k document in 6 consecutive calls of 8k tokens each, do you round each 8k piece?
- KV/prefix caching: is the crediting algorithm deterministic (would we see the same credit every month for same traffic pattern) or heuristic? We need determinism for our forecasting.
- For committed floor: will unused commit units be carried forward month-to-month, or are they true use-it-or-lose-it? The term sheet had ambiguous wording.

Last: one of our SREs flagged rare spikes where a user uploads a 120k token payload (bulk import). Will you charge us 2x or 3x the quantum for that one hit — just want to confirm worst-case billing impact.

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context-length discount mapping and token crediting — walkthrough

Emma — great questions. Below are definitive answers and a compact invoice example for the 120k case.

1) Rounding quantum: ceil applied per billed request fragment after any model-imposed chunking. Practically that means: if you stream 48k as six 8k calls, we round each 8k piece to the next multiple of 256. For the 120k single-upload (no streaming), we will split it into 256-token quanta at the meter and charge ceil(120000 / 256) = 469 quanta.

2) KV/prefix caching credits: deterministic for a given request pattern and cache TTL. Credits are calculated at request time using fixed heuristics (prefix match length, model variant compatibility). They are visible on the per-route latency/cost breakdown in the Console so you can reproduce the same credit if you replay traffic with the same keys.

3) Commit handling: unused commit units do not auto-rollover. The committed floor is applied monthly to net billed units after credits (so you are effectively billed commit price for up to the commit amount even if not consumed). We can add a negotiated rollover clause — typical enterprise concession is limited rollover (1 month) for multi-quarter deals; happy to include language if your procurement wants it.

Invoice example (list rates simplified to show mechanics):
- List price per 1k tokens: $2.50
- Meter quantum: 256 tokens
- 120,000 tokens => ceil(120000/256)=469 quanta => billed tokens = 469 * 256 = 120,064 (meters round up)
- List charge = (120,064 / 1000) * $2.50 = $300.16
- Commit discount 20% applied to charge => $240.13
- If BrightCart has KV credits worth 15% on that flow (visible as -15% line) we apply credits before floor reconciliation; final invoice line = $240.13 - (15% of $240.13) = $204.11

If the commit floor is larger than net billed units, we invoice the commit floor amount at discounted price and show a reconciliation credit or shortfall line. Example language for SOW invoice section I drafted below — let me know if you want softer wording for procurement.

SOW snippet: "Committed units are reconciled monthly. Billable units are computed after deterministic caching and crediting and rounded to the platform metering quantum (256 tokens). The committed floor will be invoiced at the committed (discounted) unit price; any overage beyond the committed amount is billed at the same discounted unit price unless otherwise negotiated."

4) Worst-case for a single 120k hit: you will be billed the rounded quanta as shown above. There is no additional penalty multiplier for long single calls; the platform does not add a long-context surcharge. The only practical impact is the rounding up to the nearest quantum.

I'll attach a one-line invoice mock (sheet 2 in the spreadsheet) and can update the SOW wording if procurement prefers rollover or different display (single line vs granular).

— Markus
